### Getting started

**URL:** https://www.notion.so/Getting-started-40e7f1ecf3344d3ba26b94865e43406f?pvs=24

**Content:**

🚀Getting startedEdited May 28🚀Getting startedOwnerVerificationEmptyTagspedago💡In this page you can find the guide to get started with our wiki, make sure you follow this guide completely.IntroductionWelcome and congratulations on becoming a cadet at 42 Heilbronn! We are really excited to have you join us and we are sure you're going to succeed!This guide will take you through the most important parts of our wiki. This wiki is the center of information here at 42 Heilbronn, here you can find almost any piece of information about stuff. Depending on when you're reading this it might be really empty or full, since it is a wiki we will be adding more stuff consistently depending on the questions and things that happen on campus. If you feel there is anything missing let us know.1. Read community rulesBefore you can start with the curriculum it’s mandatory that you read the house rules completely. You can find them here: 🤓Rules 2. Read the arrival guideWe created a guide to make it easier for you to get to 42 HN, here you can find all sort of information about housing, legal stuff, etc. You can find it here: 🗺️ Arrival Guide‣ 3. Understand the basics from 42In order to make it easier for you to get the basics from 42 we created a series of videos in which we explain to you how to what 42 is and how it works. Also you can find some extra cool stuff. Please find this videos here: 📖42 Basics

### Double Degree 42 HHN

**URL:** https://www.notion.so/42heilbronn/Double-Degree-42-HHN-79a82efba351416cbd9739efd86706cc?pvs=25

**Content:**

📚Student WikiExplore more of NotionJoin as member to collaborateJoin or create workspace📚Student Wiki👷‍♀️Internships Wiki V2              (Work Experience)Edited Aug 11👷‍♀️2 backlinksInternships Wiki V2              (Work Experience)OwnerMMarkus HagnerVerificationUntil December 31, 2025TagsEmpty💡In this page you will be able to find all the information about internships in 42, how do they work, what do we need from you and more!Table of contentsTable of contentsWhat is a 42 internship?Am I ready to start applying?Applying to internshipsPreparing for internshipI secured an internship! What are the next steps?What should I know about the internship and what happens after?Scholarships and internshipsVisa and internshipResourcesWhat is a 42 internship?After you’re done with the last circle of the core curriculum (in other words done with ft_trascendence) you need to get experience in the real world. In order to do this 42 requires you to work at a company so that you can tests your skills!There are 3 types of internships that could be valid for 42:👩‍💻Full time internship 🧑‍💻Part-time internship 👩‍💻Startup internship Inside of each page you can find more information on how the internships work, what are the requirements and what are the next steps.Am I ready to start applying?Students are ready to apply for internships when they are almost done with the core curriculum. You can consider you’re almost done when you’re 2 months before your Common Core ETA. No matter if you are in the Pace system or not you are ready for applying when only missing 1 project of circle 5 or the exam of circle 5. In order to get into the internships channel on slack and have access to the complete list of jobs and internships (pinned at the channel), please fill out the following Typeform. Additionally you will receive an invite to the CampusFounders Job_Board.and receive your official “Ready for Internship I” certificate. Thats the point to start applying.Before this time you should not be applying for internships. The main reasons for this are:You will probably find an internship before you’re done with the core curriculum, and if this happens you won’t be able to use that internship as a 42 internship meaning that it won’t count as if you were done with the core curriculumIt is only after you’re done with the core curriculum that we can assure you will have all the necessary skills to complete your job, and if we start having students going to internships before they are done with the core curriculum, this can severely damage the reputation of 42 HN and therefore make companies stop hiring our students.You will probably not have the best of the experiences in your job since you will probably not be fully prepared for it.Applying to internshipsAs we all know in 42 everyone is responsible of their own progress and internships are exactly the same. You’re responsible on creating your CV, updating your Linkedin profile, applying to companies, etc. So please don’t expect someone to be reminding you about what you should be doing.We (42 Staff Members) are always happy to help but we are not going to be pushing you to get an internship. Nevertheless we are here to help and if you have any questions or ideas please feel free to reach out to us and if we can we will be more than happy to assist you. From our side we are talking to a lot of companies to make sure that they know what 42 is and it is easier for you to apply.When applying at one of our partner companies please send your “Ready for Internship I” certificate together with your application. Also make sure you have your notifications on for the internships channel on slack, there we will be posting any update.Preparing for internshipWith your studies and completion of the core curriculum projects, you have acquired all the necessary skills to successfully launch your career.We are aware that many companies today utilize multiple programming languages, such as Python, JS/TS, Java, Rust, Go, to name just a few. Since you will likely need to work with one of these languages, we aim to provide you with the opportunity to gain foundational knowledge. This means that as soon as you are ready for the internship and have received the official 42 Heilbronn internship certificate, you will automatically be invited (at the end of the month in which you received the certificate) to participate in the following optional Cisco Courses:Python Essentials 1Python Essentials 2JavaScript Essentials 1Additionally, we will progressively introduce different learning tutorials to the curriculum, starting with Python, which you can engage with on a voluntary basis. The Python Piscine will be made available in the holy graph as soon as you complete circle 5.I secured an internship! What are the next steps?First of all congrats on securing an internship! This is an amazing milestone on anyones career, and it shouldn’t be taken lightly. Even though securing an internship is a huge step it is only the beginning, now comes doing the real work, so get ready and follow this instructions to make sure you’re all set to go:Make sure your internship offer fulfills the minimum requirements for its type (you can find more information here: 👩‍💻Full time internship, 🧑‍💻Part-time internship and 👩‍💻Startup internship)Make sure that you’re allowed to work for the whole duration of your internship. If you have a visa, please take a look into: Visa and internship Once you’re sure your internships fulfills the criteria for an internship in 42, you have to fill out the typeform in order for your project to be open.Ask Markus to open the internship project for you in case it is not openNote: We won’t open up the project unless you have submitted the previous TypeformNow follow this instructions in order to setup your internship on intra: 🤓Intranet Internships Setup Finish up your core curriculum fast to be ready to leave!What should I know about the internship and what happens after?During your internship and after it you should concentrate on the job you’re doing, 42 will contact you from time to time to get your feedback on the work you’re doing and also contact your supervisor to get feedback from company side. This will help us to learn. When starting your internship we would highly appreciate if you inform your supervisor that he will receive a short surveys from “hello@42heilbronn.de” every 2 month during your internship. Other than that there are only 3 things to remember for 42:Company evaluations on intranetMid EvaluationEnd EvaluationPeer evaluationYou will have three evaluation moments during your internship time. This consists of two evaluations with the company: one midway evaluation that happens halfway through your internship and one final evaluation at the end.To make scheduling more easy for your internship company we recommend to forward the evaluation dates at the beginning of your internship to your company contact and/or supervisor.The final evaluation to validate your internship project consists of a video that will be evaluated by your peers or a presentation that you will hold in front of your peers.Mid Evaluation:Is planned after you validate your internship contract.Will happen exactly half-way through your internship. Your supervisor will receive an automatic email on the scheduled day with a link to an evaluation form. The evaluation can also be done a few days later. End Evaluation:Will happen during the final week of your internshipYour supervisor will receive an automatic email on the scheduled day with a link to an evaluation form. The evaluation can also be done a few days later.
Pro tip: make sure your supervisor fills it in while you’re still in the company, otherwise they’ll probably forget about it and you will be stuck.Peer Evaluation Video:You have to make a video to present/show what you’ve learned. Read the subject to know how to do the video and what content to display. You need to make sure that you’re not sharing anything that’s confidential. Watch the explanatory video for more information!!!This evaluation is expected to be done on campus!Internship presentation:Instead of the peer evaluation video you can do a presentation in front of your peers.
Check the corresponding Notion page for more info: ⌚Internship Presentation Scholarships and internshipsIn case you have an active scholarship, you should send an email to hello@42heilbronn.de as soon as you can in order to define when are you leaving for the scholarship since scholarships need to suspended while you’re in an internship. This will allow us to provide scholarships to more students! Scholarships are always paid at the end of the month for the next month. In the case of an internship, you only receive your salary at the end of the month. Please note that one or more months may not be covered by the scholarship.Visa and internshipInternships for students from third countries (non-EU 42 students):In general, persons from third countries who do not have a residence permit are not allowed to work in the EU. For 42 students there is an exception for the internship at the end of the core curriculum. For this purpose, at least five weeks (not a guaranteed time frame but most of the requests were finished in that time frame) before the internship, the application form filled in by the employer must be sent to the Ausländerbehörde by Bocal. The application form can be downloaded below. As soon as you get the document back from your internship company please forward it to bocal including your contract using hello@42heilbronn.de. Only documents send by bocal will be accepted by the Ausländerbehörde. Please be aware that if you will not live in the city of Heilbronn during the course of the internship this work around will not apply. You will need to contact the respective foreigners authority in the city you will be living in. For further information about visa check back with the arrival guide. Anlage 4_Erklarung zum Besch äftigungsverhältnis_final (4).pdf3630.1KBResources42 HN Partners job offers:42 Heilbronn Internship job offers are accessible for all students. Please keep in mind that you will only be accepted as an intern at partner companies if you send your “internship ready certificate”. We like you to focus on your studies and start applying for internships when you are ready and close to be finished with the core curriculum. There is reason to be afraid not finding an internship in time.👷‍♀️Internships Wiki V2              (Work Experience)Intranet internships setup tutorial:🤓Intranet Internships Setup Company Info InternshipUnternehmen Info Praktikum engl.pdfLast modified by Markus Hagner 2 years agodrive.google.comUnternehmen Info Praktikum.pdfLast modified by Markus Hagner 2 years agodrive.google.com

  Heilbronn, Germany  From your IP address  • Update locationConversation with Gemini You're a entrepreneurship and a senior fullstack dev  I have this idea of bulding a chatbot / AI for 42 heilbronn school in Heilbronn Germany, to help new pisciners and students with their general questions, tell me in steps how to make this wrk and what you think its best, a website for this or what? Show thinkingExcellent idea. A well-designed AI assistant could be incredibly valuable for the fast-paced, high-pressure environment of the piscine and the ongoing curriculum at 42 Heilbronn.As a senior dev and entrepreneur, my advice is to start with a web-based chatbot as an MVP (Minimum Viable Product). It's the fastest way to build, test, and get feedback, while offering the most flexibility for future expansion.Here’s a step-by-step plan to make it work.Phase 1: The Lean MVP 🚀The goal here is speed and validation. You want to build something useful in a weekend or a week, not months.Step 1: Gather Your Knowledge Base (The AI's Brain)This is the most critical step. Your AI is useless without the right information. Forget complex tech for a moment and focus on the data.Create a simple document (a Markdown file in a Git repo is perfect).Brainstorm every question a pisciner asks:Logistics: "Where is the coffee machine?", "What are the cluster opening hours?", "How do I report a broken chair?"Curriculum: "What is norminette?", "How does moulinette work?", "What's the deadline for Exam 00?", "Can you explain the libft project?"Social/Rules: "Are there any student clubs?", "What are the rules for the nap room?", "Where do people go for lunch?"Get Answers: Ask current students and staff (the "Bocal") to help you answer these questions accurately. The official 42 Heilbronn resources are your source of truth.Step 2: Choose the Right (and Easiest) Tech StackYou're a full-stack dev, so you can handle this. The key is to use tools that get you to a working prototype fast.The "Brain" (LLM): Use the OpenAI Assistants API. It's designed for exactly this. You can upload your knowledge base file directly, and it handles the complex process of "Retrieval-Augmented Generation" (RAG) for you. This means the AI will use your document to answer questions, preventing it from making things up. You'll need an API key (APIkey​).Backend: A simple Node.js server with Express.js. Its only job is to receive messages from your frontend, securely call the OpenAI API with your key, and stream the response back. This is crucial—never expose your API key on the frontend.Frontend: A basic web page. You can use React (via Vite) for a fast setup. For the chat interface itself, don't build it from scratch. Use a pre-built library like react-chatbot-kit to save a massive amount of time on UI development.Step 3: Build & DeploySetup Backend: Create an Express server with one endpoint (e.g., /ask). This endpoint takes a user's question, forwards it to your OpenAI Assistant, and returns the answer.Setup Frontend: Create a simple React app with your chosen chatbot UI component. When a user sends a message, make a fetch request to your /ask endpoint on your backend.Deploy: Get it online immediately. Use services like Vercel (for the frontend) and Render (for the Node.js backend). They have generous free tiers and are incredibly easy to set up with a GitHub repository.You now have a working MVP. Share the link with a few friends at 42 and get feedback.Phase 2: Scale & Integrate 🧠Once your MVP is validated and people find it useful, it's time to make it truly powerful.Step 1: Deep Integration with the 42 EcosystemThis is the game-changer. Use the 42 Intra API.Personalization: Allow students to log in via their 42 account (OAuth). Now your chatbot can answer personalized questions like:"What's my correction point count?""Who are my evaluators for my current project?""When is my next exam?"Real-time Info: Pull data on project deadlines, Holy Graph updates, and campus events directly from the source.Step 2: Upgrade Your Knowledge BaseA single file won't scale.Vector Database: Move your knowledge base from a text file to a vector database like Pinecone, ChromaDB, or Supabase pgvector. This allows for much faster and more semantically accurate searching over a huge amount of data. You can feed it the entire 42 documentation, student-written guides, etc.CMS for Updates: Create a simple admin interface (or use a headless CMS like Strapi) so that authorized people (maybe even trusted students or staff) can update the bot's knowledge without needing to code.Step 3: Proactive FeaturesDon't just answer questions—anticipate needs.Notifications: "Heads up, your project deadline is in 48 hours."Event Reminders: "Don't forget the workshop on Docker happening in Cluster 1 at 3 PM today."Platform Choice: Website vs. OthersHere’s a breakdown of why a website is the best starting point.Website (The Winner for an MVP) 🏆Pros:Universal Access: Works on any device with a browser. No installation needed. Perfect for a quick check on a cluster Mac or a personal phone.Easy to Share: Just a URL. You can create a QR code and stick it all over the cluster.Full Control: You own the user experience, branding, and feature set.Embeddable: You can later offer the chatbot as a widget to be embedded in other community sites.Cons:Lacks the "push notification" power of a native app (though web push notifications are possible).Slack/Discord BotThis is a strong contender for a Phase 2 feature, but not for the start.Pros:Meets Users Where They Are: The 42 Heilbronn community likely lives on Slack or Discord.Excellent for Notifications: Great for pushing announcements.Cons:Limited UI: You're constrained by the chat platform's UI elements."Noise" Factor: The bot's valuable answers can get lost in a busy channel.Discovery: New students might not know which channel to find the bot in.Native Mobile App (iOS/Android)Avoid this for now.Pros:Best User Experience: Smooth, fast, and fully integrated with the OS (e.g., push notifications).Cons:Massive Overkill for an MVP: You'd have to build, maintain, and deploy two separate codebases (or use a cross-platform framework, which has its own complexities).High Barrier to Entry: Forcing a pisciner to download an app from the App Store just to ask a question is a huge friction point. They will likely just ask a human instead.Start with the website, make it awesome, and then build a Slack/Discord bot that hooks into the same backend logic. Good luck! The data that already some 42 is providing is from Notions, can this be usefull, website it is then  I want ot build it using Cursor IDE, give me a good promtp to copy and paste there to start this  Show thinkingOf course. The fact that the data is on Notion is excellent news. It's structured, and you can easily export it, which simplifies the knowledge-gathering phase immensely.Here is a comprehensive prompt designed for an AI-powered IDE like Cursor. It outlines the entire project structure, specifies the technology, and details the core logic. This will give the AI a strong, opinionated blueprint to generate a robust starting point for your application.How to Use This Prompt in CursorCreate a new, empty folder on your computer (e.g., 42-chatbot).Open that folder in Cursor.Open the chat/prompt panel (e.g., Cmd+K or Ctrl+K).Copy the entire prompt below and paste it into Cursor's chat.Let it generate the file structure and code. After it's done, follow the setup instructions I've included below the prompt.The Prompt for Cursor IDEYou are an expert full-stack developer tasked with scaffolding a complete web application. The goal is to build an AI chatbot for students at 42 Heilbronn.

**Overall Goal:**
Create a modern, scalable, and secure web application with a separate frontend and backend.

**Project Structure:**
Generate a monorepo structure with two main directories: `/client` for the frontend and `/server` for the backend.

/ (root)
├── client/         (React + Vite + Tailwind CSS)
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── components/
│   │   │   ├── ChatWindow.jsx
│   │   │   └── Message.jsx
│   │   ├── App.jsx
│   │   └── index.css
│   ├── index.html
│   └── package.json
└── server/         (Node.js + Express)
    ├── knowledge_base.md
    ├── .env
    ├── .gitignore
    ├── server.js
    └── package.json

---

### **1. Backend Details (`/server`)**

**File: `server/package.json`**
- Dependencies: `express`, `openai`, `cors`, `dotenv`, `fs` (built-in).

**File: `server/.env`**
- Create a placeholder for the OpenAI API key: `OPENAI_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY_HERE"`

**File: `server/.gitignore`**
- Add `node_modules` and `.env`.

**File: `server/knowledge_base.md`**
- Create this file and populate it with placeholder markdown content. Include a comment at the top: `<!-- Export your Notion pages to Markdown and paste the content here. This file will serve as the AI's primary knowledge source. -->`
- Example Content:
  ```markdown
  # 42 Heilbronn - Student FAQ

  ## Logistics
  - **Opening Hours**: The cluster is open 24/7.
  - **Coffee**: The main coffee machine is located in the lounge area on the ground floor. It is free of charge.

  ## Piscine
  - **Norminette**: A coding standard checker used at 42. All projects must comply with the norm. Run `norminette` on your files to check them.
  - **Moulinette**: The automated grading system that will evaluate your projects. It is merciless.
File: server/server.jsTechnology: Node.js with Express.Setup:Import express, openai, cors, dotenv, and fs.Configure dotenv to load environment variables.Initialize an Express app and enable cors and the express.json() middleware.Knowledge Loading:On server start, synchronously read the entire knowledge_base.md file into a string variable called knowledgeBase.System Prompt Construction:Create a systemPrompt string that combines instructions with the loaded knowledge. This is crucial for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).JavaScriptconst systemPrompt = `You are a helpful AI assistant for new students and pisciners at 42 Heilbronn. Your name is 'CADET-BOT'. Answer the user's questions accurately and concisely based ONLY on the context provided below. Do not use any external knowledge. If the answer is not found in the context, politely state that you don't have information on that topic.

--- CONTEXT ---
${knowledgeBase}
--- END CONTEXT ---
`;
API Endpoint:Create a POST endpoint at /api/chat.Logic:Get the user's message from the request body.Instantiate the OpenAI client using the API key from .env.Make a call to the OpenAI Chat Completions API (client.chat.completions.create).Payload:model: "gpt-4-turbo"messages: An array containing two messages:{ role: 'system', content: systemPrompt }{ role: 'user', content: message }Extract the assistant's reply from the response.Send the reply back to the client as JSON: { "reply": "..." }.Include robust error handling with a try...catch block.Server Start:Listen on a port (e.g., 3001) specified in an environment variable or defaulting. Log a confirmation message to the console.2. Frontend Details (/client)Setup: Use Vite to scaffold a React project with SWC.Styling: Use Tailwind CSS. Generate a tailwind.config.js and a postcss.config.js, and include the @tailwind directives in src/index.css.File: client/src/App.jsxShould contain the main layout: a dark background, a centered container for the chat interface, a title like "42 Heilbronn AI Assistant", and render the <ChatWindow /> component.File: client/src/components/ChatWindow.jsxThis is the core UI component.State:messages: An array of message objects, e.g., [{ sender: 'user', text: 'Hello' }, { sender: 'ai', text: 'Hi!' }].isLoading: A boolean to show a loading indicator while waiting for the AI's response.UI:A message display area that maps over the messages state and renders a <Message /> component for each one. This area should be scrollable.An input form at the bottom with a text input and a "Send" button.Functionality:An async function handleSendMessage that is called on form submission.Logic of handleSendMessage:Prevent default form submission.Get the user's message from the input. If it's empty, do nothing.Update the messages state to include the user's new message.Set isLoading to true.Make a POST request to the backend's /api/chat endpoint, sending the user's message in the body.When the response is received, create a new AI message object.Update the messages state again, adding the AI's reply.Set isLoading to false.Clear the input field.File: client/src/components/Message.jsxA simple component that takes a message object as a prop.It should render the message text with different styling based on whether the sender is 'user' or 'ai'. For example, user messages are on the right with a blue background, and AI messages are on the left with a gray background.
---

### Your Next Steps After Generation

1.  **Install Dependencies:** Run `npm install` inside the `/client` directory and then again inside the `/server` directory.
2.  **Set API Key:** Open `/server/.env` and replace `"YOUR_API_KEY_HERE"` with your actual OpenAI API key.
3.  **Populate Knowledge Base:** Open `/server/knowledge_base.md`. Go to your Notion pages, export them as Markdown, and paste the content into this file. The more detailed it is, the smarter your bot will be.
4.  **Run the Application:**
    * In one terminal, navigate to `/server` and run `node server.js`.
    * In a second terminal, navigate to `/client` and run `npm run dev`.
5.  **Open the App:** Your browser should open to the Vite development server (usually `http://localhost:5173`). You should see your chatbot interface, ready to go!
 how to export notions from a workplace, thats not mine of course Show thinkingThis is a very important and sensitive question. As an AI assistant, and in my role as your "senior dev/entrepreneur" advisor, I must be very clear about this:You absolutely should not, and technically cannot, export data from a Notion workspace that you do not own or have been given explicit export permissions for.Attempting to access or export data without authorization is a serious issue for several reasons:Ethical & Legal: It's a violation of trust and privacy. In Germany, this falls under strict data privacy laws (DSGVO/GDPR). Unauthorized data access can have significant legal consequences.Intellectual Property: The content within the 42 Heilbronn Notion workspace is the property of the organization.Notion's Terms of Service: Bypassing security or access controls is a direct violation of Notion's policies and could lead to account suspension.Technical Barriers: Notion is designed to prevent this. Export functionality is tied to the permissions of your user account. If you're not an admin or haven't been given full access, the options will be disabled.The Right Approach: The Entrepreneur's WayYour goal is to get the data to help the community. The professional and correct way to do this is not to find a technical workaround, but to build a bridge and get official collaboration.Here is a step-by-step plan to get the data you need, the right way.Step 1: Identify the Owner(s)Find out who manages the Notion workspace. It is likely the Bocal (the staff) or a specific person in charge of student resources.Step 2: Prepare Your PitchYou are building a valuable tool for the school, for free. Frame your request as a collaboration that benefits everyone. You need to present your project clearly and professionally.What is it? "I am developing an AI-powered chatbot to help new and current students answer common questions about 42 Heilbronn."What is the benefit for them? "This will reduce the number of repetitive questions the staff receives, help pisciners feel more supported, and serve as a 24/7 accessible resource for everyone."What do you need? "To ensure the chatbot is accurate and trustworthy, I need to use the official information currently stored in the school's Notion workspace as its knowledge base."How will it work? "I can use a one-time export of the relevant pages, or, for a more advanced solution, we could use the Notion API for read-only access to keep the information automatically up-to-date."Step 3: Make the Formal RequestDraft a professional email or schedule a meeting.Here is a template you can adapt:Subject: Proposal for a 42 Heilbronn AI Assistant & Collaboration RequestHello [Name of Bocal/Admin],My name is [Your Name], and I am a student here at 42 Heilbronn.I am currently developing a project to benefit the entire student community: an AI-powered chatbot designed to instantly answer common questions for pisciners and students. The goal is to create a helpful, 24/7 resource that can provide information on everything from cluster logistics and curriculum details to campus life. I believe this could significantly improve the onboarding experience and reduce the repetitive query load on staff.To ensure the bot's reliability, its knowledge base must be built from the official source of truth, which I understand is the school's Notion workspace.Would it be possible to discuss how I could get access to this information? A one-time export of the relevant public-facing pages in Markdown format would be perfect for the initial version.I am happy to provide a demo of my current progress and discuss the project in more detail at your convenience.Thank you for your time and consideration.Best regards,[Your Name]
[Your Intra Login]How Exporting Works (When You Have Permission)Once you have permission, the process is straightforward. The workspace admin can do one of the following for you:Option 1: Manual Export (Best for MVP)This is the simplest method. The admin navigates to the page(s) you need, and does the following:Clicks the three-dot menu (...) in the top-right corner of a Notion page.Selects "Export".Chooses "Markdown & CSV" as the export format. This is perfect for your knowledge_base.md file.Includes subpages if necessary.Clicks "Export" and sends you the resulting ZIP file.Option 2: Workspace Export (Admin Only)If they want to give you everything, an admin can export the entire workspace from "Settings & Members" > "Settings" > "Export all workspace content". This creates a ZIP file of all pages.Option 3: Granting You Access (The Collaborative Way)They could create a specific role for you or share the relevant pages with your Notion account with "Can view" or "Full access" permissions, which would then allow you to perform the export yourself.Option 4: Using the Notion API (The Pro Way for Phase 2)For your scaling phase, you could request to build a Notion API integration. This would allow your application to fetch data programmatically and always be up-to-date. This is more complex but is the most sustainable solution.By approaching this through official channels, you not only get the data you need but also build credibility, gain potential allies for your project, and ensure you are creating a tool that is approved and supported by the school.
